summary: Adjudicated the algebraic-stack wiring question empirically. The recorded elaboration-conflict hazard does NOT reproduce for the four orphaned Algebraic/ modules: an adversarial build importing the aggregator directly into BXCanonical/Completeness.lean re-elaborated Completeness, CompletenessDedekind and StrongCompleteness with rc=0 and zero errors. Recommendation is option (a), re-wire via one import in FormalSystem/Metalogic.lean; measured marginal cost 5.3s elaboration and 948 KB olean. Confirmed all README overstatements plus three further doc inaccuracies.

artifacts.summary: Recommends re-wiring the Algebraic aggregator into Metalogic.lean; refutes the elaboration-conflict hazard empirically and specifies seven README/manifest corrections.

decisions_made: Recommend option (a) re-wire: the isolation rationale does not survive measurement and the cost is 5.3s elaboration / 948 KB olean
Wire at FormalSystem/Metalogic.lean (downstream), not at BXCanonical/Completeness.lean: both build green, but the downstream position does not falsely assert that completeness depends on the algebra
Import the aggregator rather than the deepest leaf, so all five manifest entries clear and the aggregator itself becomes lake-verified
Do not widen scope to Core.lean / Bundle.lean / SoundnessLemmas.lean: same manifest block, but each needs its own cycle analysis and none was tested
dead_ends: Git archaeology cannot explain the original hazard as an import-graph effect: at commit 1961830e2 neither Completeness.lean nor Metalogic.lean imported the aggregator, so the recorded interference has uncertain provenance
Cold full-build wall time was not measured (would require discarding the entire 484 MB FormalSystem build cache), so the build delta is reported in absolute terms rather than as a percentage
